checks: Checked source §4. For left replacement, projection of the positive-gain set gives old domination lπ, new left domination mℓ, and equal second marginals. Thus the stated scaling controls both feasibility and gain; interchanging sides proves the second estimate.

The double projection has old domination lsπ and new marginal dominations msℓ and mlr. The maximum of these coefficients suffices, and a zero unused marginal makes the integral zero without division. Exact optimality forces each positive part to vanish almost everywhere.
Among probability couplings of π_X/m and π_Y/m the normalized plan has gap at most ε/m, since each competitor multiplied by m is feasible for the partial class. Scaling π^{⊗k} back yields km^{k−1}ε.

dependencies.hypotheses: The selected normalized marginal laws are probability laws on compact metric spaces, the same Borel cost is bounded, and their fixed-marginal gap is at most ε/m.

overlap.comparison: Covers the cyclic fixed-marginal portion by scaling. It has no unused-endpoint capacity terms and does not imply the three new exchange bounds.

review_method: Independent cold proof read, source-locator comparison, predecessor proof comparison, and exact arithmetic replay where relevant.
summary: All three free endpoint exchange estimates and the rescaled cyclic estimate hold for bounded Borel costs.
